title: ESR investigation of starch gelatinization using novel spin probes
abstract: AbstractThe spin probes 1,1,3,3‐tetramethylisoindolin‐2‐yloxyl (TMIO) and the sodium salt of its sulfonate, 1,1,3,3‐tetramethylisoindolin‐2‐yloxyl‐5‐sulfonate (NaTMIOS) were used to monitor the microviscosity changes of water during starch gelatinization. In cereal starch, which contains mainly A‐type polymorphs, evidence was found for the amylopectin and amylose regions, the latter undergoing a transition at about 55 °C and a large increase in the microviscosity on cooling. Pea starch contains both A‐and B‐type polymorphs and this was also found to have two domains and the 55 °C transition was observed for the amylose phase: the less mobile amylopectin showed a reversible decrease in water microviscosity on heating.
